The state government urged banks to increase lending within the state, clear pending loan applications and improve credit access, particularly under the Kisan Credit Card and PM Vishwakarma schemes. Credit-Deposit Ratio The Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR) is the ratio of a bank's total loans and advances to its total deposits, expressed as a percentage. bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI, Motihari Promotes Sustainable Orchard Management under Khet Bachao ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 27 October 2026, East Champaran, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organised a farmer awareness and field interaction programme under Khet Bachao Abhiyan 2026 at Kothia Hariram village, Mehsi Block, East Champaran, today. The programme focused on promoting judicious fertilizer use, soil health management, nutrient recycling, crop diversification and sustainable management of mango and litchi orchards. The programme under Khet Bachao Abhiyan 2026 emphasized soil-test-based nutrient management, balanced fertilization and sustainable orchard management to enhance mango and litchi productivity while maintaining long-term soil fertility. Farmers were sensitized to the importance of recycling organic resources such as crop residues, fallen leaves, farmyard manure and compost, along with the judicious use of mineral fertilizers. The programme also highlighted intercropping and crop diversification as strategies to improve land-use efficiency, generate supplementary income and strengthen farmers’ livelihoods. Emphasis was placed on efficient resource utilization, reduced input costs, improved soil health and enhanced resilience to climatic and economic uncertainties. Interactive discussions addressed farmers’ challenges and promoted practical, economically viable and environmentally sustainable orchard management practices. Through this initiative, ICAR-MGIFRI reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable horticulture, soil health and farmers’ self-reliance in the mango- and litchi-growing regions of East Champaran, Bihar. A total of 29 farmers and participants attended the programme and interacted on improved orchard management and efficient utilization of locally available resources. bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 1 min Read Bihar to seek Centre's aid to clear flood-hit farmlands, fisheries of sand and silt The state Disaster Management Department (DMD) has asked district magistrates (DMs) of 22 districts to assess sand and silt deposits on flood-affected agricultural land and fisheries caused by the floods in Ganga, Son, Gandak, Kosi and other rivers. PTI Published On Oct 27, 2026 at 08:55 PM IST Select ETGovernment as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment The worst-affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. The Bihar government will seek funds from the Centre to remove sand and silt from farmlands and fisheries affected in the recent floods in the state, an official statement said on Tuesday. The state Disaster Management Department (DMD) has asked district magistrates (DMs) of 22 districts to assess sand and silt deposits on flood-affected agricultural land and fisheries caused by the floods in Ganga, Son, Gandak, Kosi and other rivers. "Acting on the chief minister's directions, the DMD has written to the DMs of Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura, Arwal, West and East Champaran, Gopalganj, Darbhanga, Muzaffarpur, Supaul and Saharsa, directing them to assess sand and silt deposits on agricultural land and in fisheries affected by recent floods," the statement said. The department asked authorities concerned to conduct on-site inspection of the affected agricultural land and fisheries and assess the extent of sand and silt deposition. "Based on this assessment, financial assistance will be sought in accordance with prescribed relief norms of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)," it said. This assistance will help restore and facilitate agricultural and fisheries-related activities in the affected areas, it added. Around 50 lakh people across several Bihar districts were affected by the recent floods, which also damaged agricultural land and fisheries, officials said. The worst-affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. This train, numbered 19427/19428, will start operations ahead of Diwali, and will run between Gujarat's Bhuj and Bihar's Barauni. Its total route will be 2,532-km long and will connect four states, namely, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar. However, the PM's official itinerary does not mention this train inauguration. Modi will be on a two-day Gujarat visit from October 30 during which he will inaugurate and launch development projects of Banas Dairy and attend the National Unity Day parade at the Statue of Unity, the state government said on Tuesday, as per news agency PTI. Service to operate thrice a week The 19427 Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express will depart from Bhuj at 5:30 pm and will take 58 hours and 35 minutes to reach Barauni. While returning, the 19428 Barauni-Bhuj Amrit Bharat Express will depart at 11:55 at tnight and reach Bhij at 1:15 pm on the fourth day after journey of 61 hours and 20 minutes. The Bhuj-Barauni service will operate on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, while the Barauni-Bhuj service will operate on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Which are some of the major stations this service will connect? The new service will have commercial stoppages at several important stations en route, including Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur, among others. The new train service will provide an additional rail travel option between western and eastern parts of the country and improve connectivity for passengers travelling between Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. With the train launching ahead of Diwali , it is expected to benefit a large number of workers from UP and Bihar who are employed in Gujarat's industrial centres like Kutch, Ahmedabad, Morbi, and Vadodara. Amrit Bharat Express: What does it offer? The Amrit Bharat Express is a modern non-AC long-distance sleeper class train for affordable travel within India. These trains come with 11 General Class coaches, 8 Sleeper Class coaches, 1 Pantry Car, and 2 Second Class–cum–Luggage–cum–Guard Vans with disabled-friendly compartments. Fares are generally ₹ 500 for every 1,000 km, and there is no dynamic pricing, thus ensuring accessibility for the common passenger. As per the railways, this enhanced connectivity supports employment mobility, tourism, trade, and access to education and healthcare. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar e-Challans Now Block RC Renewal, Fitness Certificates and Transfers Breaking News Bihar e-Challans Now Block RC Renewal, Fitness Certificates and Transfers By Harpreet Singh October 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar will restrict key transport services for vehicles with unpaid e-challans, including registration certificate renewal, fitness certification and ownership transfers, under enforcement instructions issued by the state transport department on October 27. State transport commissioner Arif Ahsan directed district transport officers and other concerned authorities to act against vehicles with pending traffic fines in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions. Vehicles with unpaid dues may also be blacklisted on the transport department’s online portal until the fines are cleared. The restrictions will cover renewal of registration certificates, issuance of duplicate RCs and updates to a vehicle owner’s correspondence address. The department will also stop ownership transfers for vehicles with outstanding e-challans, preventing owners from selling or formally transferring such vehicles until the dues are settled. “Under the new enforcement measures, online transport services linked to vehicles with unpaid e-challans will be restricted,” Ahsan said. He added that issuance of fitness certificates and other related documents would also be affected. The department has further ordered restrictions on pollution certificates and updated repair or fitness-related certificates where vehicles have pending fines. The measures will apply to vehicles identified through the transport portal and will be supported by regular and random checks by enforcement officials. The action is also intended to target repeat traffic offenders. Officials have been instructed to act against driving licence holders who repeatedly violate traffic rules, including suspension of licences and restrictions on renewal wherever applicable. If a vehicle is found during a check to have an unpaid or non-complied e-challan, officials may seize it under applicable provisions. Transport Secretary Raj Kumar said effective enforcement of traffic rules was essential to improving road safety. He said action against vehicles with pending e-challans would be taken in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions, adding that the objective was not only to recover fines but also to promote responsibility and discipline among motorists, reduce traffic violations and help prevent road accidents. The instructions place online transport services at the centre of Bihar’s traffic-fine enforcement system. A pending challan can now affect several routine vehicle transactions, including documentation, certification and ownership changes, rather than remaining only an unpaid penalty. Ahsan directed officials to conduct regular and random checks, identify vehicles with pending challans and take action under the prescribed provisions. The department’s instructions did not specify a separate deadline for vehicle owners to clear existing dues before the restrictions take effect. The Yarlung Tsangpo flows from Tibet into Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called as the Siang, before joining other rivers to form the Brahmaputra in Assam. Since China's project is situated upstream, Indian authorities are intrigued about the possible impact of reservoir operations on downstream water flows. Although a dam cannot simply stop the Brahmaputra's flow, its operation could impact the timing and volume of water releases. This has ignited concerns about seasonal water availability, instant discharges and flood management. national_raw_news.title: Polling underway in Israel to elect new Parliament
national_raw_news.content: Polling is underway across Israel, with voters choosing representatives to the country’s 120-member Knesset. With 7.3 million eligible voters and 36 parties contesting the election, the outcome will determine the balance of power in parliament. Voting will end at 10 pm local time tonight. The election comes amid intense debate over national security, the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, military service and the country’s future political direction. The election is widely viewed as a test of Netanyahu’s leadership, with opposition figures, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to challenge his right-wing coalition. Israel follows a nationwide proportional representation system in which the entire country constitutes a single electoral constituency. Political parties must secure at least 3.25% of the national vote to enter the Knesset. Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 years across three separate periods since 1996. Former Israel Defence Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party, has emerged as one of Netanyahu’s principal challengers. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett is leading the B’Yachad electoral alliance, which includes former prime minister Yair Lapid’s Yesh Atid party. Other significant political players include Yair Golan’s left-leaning Democrats, Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu and Arab-led parties such as Ra’am and the Joint List.

national_raw_news.content: The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concluded today with the adoption of the Joint Declaration unanimously. Mr. Birla said that despite differences in opinions, backgrounds and challenges, BRICS countries share a common commitment to human welfare, peace and prosperity. Mr. Birla emphasised the need to respect the sovereignty of every nation, resolve international disputes peacefully and ensure equitable development opportunities for all. The Lok Sabha Speaker said that during the two-day forum, the discussions focused not only on current challenges but also on exploring new avenues for future cooperation. Highlighting the prevailing global conflicts, regional instability and economic uncertainty, Mr. Birla stressed that dialogue and cooperation are more important than ever. He said India believes that lasting solutions to global problems can be achieved through dialogue rather than conflict, peace rather than war, and cooperation rather than competition. He added that global peace must guarantee security, dignity and justice, along with the promise of a better future for everyone, particularly the younger generation. Mr Birla said that through the joint declaration, the participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of the United Nations Charter, sovereign equality of nations, mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of international disputes. He said, the declaration also strongly condemned all acts of terrorism and called for coordinated and concrete action against all terrorists and terrorist organisations. Emphasising the use of Artificial Intelligence, Mr. Birla said its application should be guided by the principles of ethics, transparency, accountability and human welfare. He stressed that technology should improve human life and its development must remain aligned with human values. Mr. Birla said the success of BRICS should not be limited to the progress of its member countries but should also have a positive impact on the wider global community. He emphasised that the aspirations of the Global South must receive due consideration in global decision-making processes. national_raw_news.title: EC defends SIR of electoral rolls before Supreme Court
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission has defended its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls before the Supreme Court, maintaining that the exercise was authorised by law and the relevant orders were approved unanimously by all three members of the Commission. Rejecting the allegations that Form 6 had been amended, the poll panel, in its 248-page response to the petition against the chief election commissioner (CEC), said that no changes were made to the statutory Form 6 used for voter registration. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear on Tuesday petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the decisions taken by the poll panel during the SIR. In a counter-affidavit, the poll body sought summary dismissal of the petitions and called the allegations misconceived, which rested on a single newspaper report. The affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the Commission said attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members of the Commission. The Affidavit said the three SIR orders were issued in accordance with decisions of the EC arrived at unanimously and taken in due compliance with Article 324 of the Constitution of India. The poll body said any suggestion, observation or query raised by a commissioner while a file is being processed does not constitute a decision of the Commission. On the Form 6 row, the EC said it unequivocally rejects the misleading contention that the statutory form had been changed. It added that Form 6 is an application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral rolls According to the affidavit, the declaration attached during the SIR is a separate document provided by the SIR orders and “is not a part of Form 6. It said the declaration used in the Bihar SIR was later replaced in the subsequent orders so that applicants could give details of themselves and their parents or grandparents from the 2002-03 rolls and avoid submitting further documents once successfully mapped. The poll body also said that appeals filed in West Bengal against orders including electors in the rolls were filed by officers of the state chief electoral officer’s office acting as statutory authorities in line with the apex court’s orders, and that ” matters were not brought to the Commission. Questioning the maintainability of the pleas, the Commission said, in the eyes of law, a newspaper report is not treated as evidence of the facts it narrates. The Commission added that it has “neither released nor authorised the release of any internal note/ file to any news agency. Citing Article 324(5) of the Constitution, which protects the CEC from removal except in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, the EC said any prayer to restrain the CEC from functioning was not maintainable. It also rejected the petitioner’s contentions on electronic voting machines (EVMs). The EC said similar challenges had been rejected by the top court several times.

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas Eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a fee plaza can avail Concessional Local Pass for Rs. 1,500 per annum for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs. 3,000 per annum for fee plazas situated within these limits depending on the location of the plaza Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi In a major step to enhance ‘Ease of Living’ for citizens residing near National Highway Fee Plazas, the Government of India has introduced a ‘Concessional Local Pass’ for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The rule will come into effect from 01 st November 2026. The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits. Under the new provision, eligible non-commercial vehicle owners with a valid and functional FASTag, residing within 20 km range can choose between the existing monthly pass and the concessional Local Pass for commuting through a specific fee plaza. The pass will be valid only for that fee plaza and will not be transferable to any other plazas. The concessional Local Pass will not be available on National Highways or Expressways where toll fee collection is based on a closed user-fee collection system. It will also not be issued where a service road or alternative road is available for use by commuters. The Annual Local Pass will be available at eligible Toll Plazas wef 01.11.2026. The Annual Local Pass will also be available through Rajmargyatra App wef 01.12.2026. The amendment has been notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the powers conferred by the National Highways Act, 1956. The rates may be revised by the Central Government annually with revisions taking effect on 01 st April. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship. The journey of Mohan Lal (name changed) , a 65-year-old waste picker from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, highlights how social protection and healthcare support can help vulnerable workers overcome serious medical challenges and move towards a healthier life. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, Mohan Lal spent most of his life working as a contractual sanitation worker and waste picker, earning between Rs 101 and Rs 250 per day. His modest income was barely sufficient to meet his family’s basic needs, leaving little scope for savings or unexpected expenses. When he was diagnosed with a serious heart blockage requiring specialised treatment, the high cost of medical care became a major concern for him and his family. Enrolled under the Waste Pickers component of the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, Mohan Lal received an Ayushman Card under Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY). This support enabled him to access treatment for his heart blockage at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, on 8 May 2026, with the full cost of his medical treatment covered. Following successful treatment, Mohan Lal recovered and was able to return to work and resume supporting his family. Access to healthcare eased the financial burden associated with his medical emergency and helped him focus on recovery. The timely intervention also restored his confidence and provided renewed hope for the future. Mohan Lal’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible healthcare and social protection for waste pickers and other vulnerable workers. His recovery reflects how welfare initiatives can help reduce barriers to essential medical treatment, safeguard dignity and strengthen family well-being. His story stands as an encouraging example of how timely support can help individuals move beyond difficult circumstances and look towards the future with renewed confidence. *** SS-149-TAR/KV/GA/RK (Release ID: 2329130) Visitor Counter : 95 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी Share -- words | -- min read Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship. According to a press release from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Mandaviya assured the Bureau of India’s commitment to clean sport. He said, “India firmly believes that sporting excellence must always be accompanied by integrity. Every athlete deserves a fair opportunity to compete, with success determined by talent, preparation and hard work, and not by prohibited substances or methods. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has regularly emphasised clean sport and the need to practice zero tolerance towards the menace of doping.” The Union Sports Minister highlighted the strengthening of India’s anti-doping framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment. “India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “We will also bring another amendment in the next session of our parliament, which aims to introduce criminal provisions to deal with violations even more effectively, including those by coaches and supply chain stakeholders,” he said. The Union Sports Minister further highlighted the steps India has already taken to tackle doping and inform its athletes about banned substances. “During 2025-26, the National Anti-Doping Agency of India conducted over 7,000 tests and more than 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching 27,000 participants, while focusing on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “The Know Your Medicine mobile application has recorded over half a million searches, supporting informed decisions about medicines,” he said. Mandaviya highlighted the forthcoming signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Ministry of Education, and UNESCO to introduce the Sport Values in Every Classroom Toolkit in India. The agenda also covered resource mobilisation, the Fund’s Operational Strategy for 2026-2031, compliance and capacity-building to support a sustainable global anti-doping system. national_raw_news.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Be Held At Dilli Haat, New Delhi, From November 1 To 15
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Be Held At Dilli Haat, New Delhi, From November 1 To 15 ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’ To Celebrate India’s Traditional Crafts, Festive Lighting And Cultural Heritage Showcasing Artisan Products, Traditional Craftsmanship and Cultural Programmes through Seven Thematic Zones Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi The fortnight long Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will be organized at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, from November 1 to 15, 2026. The Mela is being organized by the Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment. Themed ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the event will celebrate India’s traditional crafts, festive lighting and cultural heritage through artisan products, live craft demonstrations and cultural programmes. A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela continues the Ministry’s efforts to provide aspirational groups and communities with a platform to showcase their creativity, talent and traditional craftsmanship, while creating opportunities to market their products to a wider audience. He said since 2022, the Shilp Samagam Melas have benefited more than 1,000 artisans. The Official said this year, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) (DEPwD) will organise Shilp Utsav together for the first time, with approximately 150 stalls under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest. The collaboration will bring together traditional artisans, creative talent and inclusive participation in a shared platform. The Ministry Official said the Mela will be curated around seven thematic zones showcasing India’s crafts, traditions, food and cultural expressions. कला आँगन will feature live craft demonstrations; प्रकाश चौक will showcase lamps and lights; पूजा पथ will present devotional products; सजावट बाज़ार will focus on home décor; घराना will feature textiles and fashion; स्वाद चौक will offer food; and मंच will host cultural activities and performances. The Official further said that Bharat TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) is an initiative aimed at marketing products made by aspirational groups to consumers in India and abroad through e-commerce platforms. The programme seeks to support economic empowerment while contributing to the preservation of India’s traditional arts and crafts, he added. The Ministry Official said the Purple Fest is a multidimensional celebration of disability, creativity, talent and equal participation. It brings together persons with disabilities, organisations, institutions, businesses, artists, professionals and other stakeholders to celebrate achievements, encourage participation and promote greater understanding of inclusion, he further said. Through Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, the Ministry seeks to provide greater visibility to traditional artisans and their products while celebrating India’s rich cultural heritage and encouraging wider public engagement with craftsmanship, creativity and inclusive participation. national_raw_news.title: Under Secretary assesses progress of Special Campaign 6.0 at vital Orgs under MoI&B
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News Under Secretary assesses progress of Special Campaign 6.0 at vital Orgs under MoI&B ITANAGAR, Oct 26: Shivram Meena, Under Secretary (BP&L), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoI&B), Government of India, visited Akashvani, Doordarshan Kendra (DDK), the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Itanagar today to review the progress of Special Campaign 6.0. During the visit, Meena interacted with officers and staff members and reviewed the initiatives undertaken by the respective offices under the campaign. The review focused on cleanliness and upkeep of office premises, management and disposal of e-waste, record management, optimal utilisation of office space and measures to improve administrative efficiency. He emphasised the importance of maintaining cleanliness in the workplace and sustaining the initiatives undertaken as part of the campaign. At Akashvani (Itanagar), the MoI&B official visited the campus and interacted with officers and staff members to review the initiatives undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0. He took stock of the cleanliness and upkeep of the premises, office management practices, record maintenance and utilisation of available infrastructure. During the visit, he also participated in a brief plantation activity, highlighting the importance of environmental conservation and maintaining green surroundings. At DDK, Meena inspected the studios, administrative offices, news and programme sections, record-keeping systems and other facilities. He also assessed the upkeep of the campus, interacted with officers and staff members, and stressed the need to maintain a clean and orderly working environment. He subsequently visited the CBC and the PIB, Regional Office, Itanagar, and reviewed the cleanliness and upkeep of the offices and the progress of activities undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0. He interacted with officials and staff members and took stock of the measures adopted for effective office management, record maintenance and e-waste disposal. Meena also visited the FTII, Itanagar, and reviewed the cleanliness and upkeep of the campus and the initiatives undertaken as part of Special Campaign 6.0. The Registrar and faculty members of FTII, Itanagar, accompanied him during the visit. He interacted with them and discussed measures relating to cleanliness, efficient utilisation of institutional infrastructure, record management and the maintenance of a clean and organised working environment. Utsav Parmar, Joint Director, Doordarshan and Akashvani, Itanagar; Ranjan Karmarkar, Assistant Director (E) and Head of Office, Akashvani, Itanagar; and Akhilesh Kumar Dwivedi, Assistant Director (E) and Head of Office, Doordarshan Kendra, accompanied Meena during the visit. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Communications Special Campaign 6: Department of Telecommunications records notable achievements against campaign targets Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi As Special Campaign 6 enters its final week, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) along with its PSUs/Subordinate offices/Attached Offices/ Autonomous Bodies/ Other Institutions has recorded notable achievements, meeting or exceeding targets in key areas of public grievance redressal, revenue generation and space management. The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions has allocated 26.10.26 as the dedicated day for carrying out cleanliness activities across pan India offices of the Department of Telecommunications. On this dedicated day, a special drive was carried out to de-clutter office space and plantation of trees across 520 campaign sites in the Department. The Department has achieved its target for disposal of public grievances, resolving 2,270 grievances. In addition, all 640 pending public grievance appeals reported on the campaign dashboard have been disposed of. The target set for disposal of IMC references has also been fully achieved. The Department has generated Revenue of ₹2.08 crore through scrap disposal and revenue of ₹2.18 crore from e-waste disposal. The Department has so far freed 80,724 square feet of office space against a target of 45,000 square feet. These results reflect concerted efforts towards efficient record management, responsible disposal of scrap and e-waste, and better utilization of office space.
